statement:
Prove that for every positive integer $n$ there exists a unique ordered pair $(a, b)$ of positive integers such that
\[
n = \frac{1}{2}(a + b - 1)(a + b - 2) + a.
\]

Let $X = \mathbb{Z}^3$ denote the set of all triples $(a, b, c)$ of integers. Define $f : X \to X$ by
\[
f(a, b, c) = (a + b + c,\; ab + bc + ca,\; abc).
\]
Find all triples $(a, b, c)$ such that $f(f(a, b, c)) = (a, b, c)$.
Some $46$ squares are randomly chosen from a $9 \times 9$ chessboard and colored red. Show that there exists a $2 \times 2$ block of $4$ squares of which at least three are colored red.
